correctness.rationale: Character diagonalization gives the individual sphere eigenvalues via quadratic Gauss sums. The signed difference cancels the common q^(d-1) mode and complementary character classes ensure exactly one nonzero Salié term off the dual isotropic cone. For dual norm s!=0 the two roots ±v of v²=rs give q^m(ψ(v)+ψ(-v)) up to sign; s=0 yields ±2q^m. Each nonzero s has multiplicity q^(d-1)+C_Q η(s) q^m; two opposing radial classes sum to 2q^(d-1). Product over all unordered ±v in F_q^× is 2^((q/p-1)/2) via ∏_{t∈F_p}(ζ^t+ζ^-t)=2. This yields determinant, q,p-exact prime support, and all min/max abs-cosine levels. Representation of nonzero dual norms uses an isotropic hyperbolic plane in dimension>=3. Independent direct Fourier eigenvalue enumeration for q=3,5,7 in dimension 3 reproduced determinant log-products and extrema; these tests are finite only.
residual_risks: All-characteristic determinant depends on exact normalization and Gauss/Salié signs; mathematical derivation checked symbolically, finite tests not an infinite proof.

final_claim: For odd q=p^e, odd d=2m+1>=3, nonsingular quadratic Q, and nonzero opposing-character radii a,b, the signed difference sphere-convolution matrix has absolute determinant 2^(q^d/p) q^(m*q^d), smallest singular value 2q^m sin(pi/(2p)), largest 2q^m.
limitations: Odd characteristic, odd dimension >=3, nonzero radii of opposing characters, homogeneous nondegenerate Q, unnormalized convolution.
